Kabc020099932022
 In The Court Of Xxi Addl.Small Cause Judge And
 Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Bangalore.

(Scch-23)
 Dated This The 8th Day Of January - 2025
 Present: Sri. Shreyansh Doddamani
 B.Com. Ll.B, (Spl)
 Xxi Addl. Scj & Acjm
 Member - Mact, Bengaluru.

Petitioner : Sri. Yatheesha. D.H,
 S/o D.L. Huchhegowda,
 Aged about 36 years,
 R/at : No.148,
 Dasarighatta,
 Tumkur District-572201
 (By Sri.G.S. Muralidhara, Advocate)
 v/s
Respondent/s : 1. Sri. Shivakumar. C.G,
 S/o Gurubasavaiah,
 No. M-105, 5th Cross,
 7th Main, L.N. Puram,
 Sreerampura,
 Bengaluru-560021.
 (Rc owner of the car bearing
 Reg.No.KA-02-MQ-0124)
 (Exparte)
 Scch-23 2 Mvc No.1712/2022
 2. Bajaj Allianz Gen.Ins.Co.Ltd.,
 No.1/2, Golden Heights,
 4th Floor, 59th C Cross,
 4th M Block, Rajajinagar,
 Bengaluru-560010.
 (Policy No.HBZ/11748770
 Valid from 25.11.2019 to 24.11.2020)
 (By Sri.M.A. Patil Advocate)
 Judgment
This claim petition is filed under section 166 of the M.V. Act, seeking compensation for the injuries sustained in a road traffic accident.

Yatheesha D.H vs Shivakumar C.G on 8 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/93918844/
1 2.

The case of the petitioner in the nutshell is that, on 17.03.2020 at about 1.50 p.m, when the petitioner was proceeding as a pillion rider and his friend namely K.N. Rajkumar was riding the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-04-JR- 6604 and proceeding slowly and cautiously by observing all the traffic rules and regulations.

When they reached near Terige Bhavana underpass, Nagarbhavi Ring Road, Bengaluru City at that time driver of car bearing Reg.No.02-MQ-0124 came from same direction i.e., from hind side in a rash and negligent manner so as to endanger human life and without maintaining the proper distance from other vehicle dashed to the petitioner's motorcycle.

Due to tremendous impact petitioner sustained grievous injuries & immediately shifted to Essential Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he took treatment as inpatient and underwent surgery and he was discharged with an advice to regular follow-up treatment.
He further submitted that he was hale and healthy and was working as Driver in BMTC and was getting salary of Rs.27,000/- p.m.
Due to the accidental injuries he lost income from the date of accident.
It is further urged that, the accident happened because of rash and negligent driving of the driver of the car.
The respondent No.1 & 2 being the owner and insurer and they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation, as such prayed to grant a compensation amount.
3. Notice was duly served to respondent No.1, the respondent No.1 did not appear before this Tribunal.
Hence he was placed exparte.
4. The respondent No.2 appeared through his counsel and filed written statement admitted the issuance of commercial vehicle insurance policy in respect of car bearing Reg.No.KA-02- MQ-0124.
However the liability if any is pleaded to be subject to the terms & conditions of the policy.
This respondent specifically and empathically denied the occurrence, mode and manner of accident and also involvement of the vehicle in the accident.
Negligence on the part of the driver of the insured car is denied by this respondent.

Per contra it is alleged that the rider of motorcycle in which the petitioner was proceeding as pillion rider who was riding the said vehicle without having a proper lookout at the vehicular movement on the road was solely responsible for the occurrence of the accident.
Without prejudice to the said contention it is averred that the driver of the insured car not possess valid & effective DL as on the date of accident.

Further the police have filed charge sheet against the driver of car bearing Reg.No.KA-02-MQ-0124 for the offences punishable u/s 279, 337,
338 of IPC and Sec.3(1) r/w 181 of MV Act.
On account of willful breach of the terms & conditions of the policy by the insured, the insurance company is not liable to indemnify him.
Further denied all the allegation made in the petition.
Hence prayed to dismiss the petition.
Rest of the petition averments are contended as false and baseless and it is prayed to dismiss the petition.

5. On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues were framed :
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioner proves that he sustained injuries in a road traffic accident that occurred on 17.03.2020 at about 1.50 p.m., when the petitioner was traveling from Nagarbhavi towards Summanahalli Bridge, Near Terige Bhavan, due to actionable negligence of the driver of the car bearing Reg.No.KA-02-MQ-0124 ?
Yatheesha D.H vs Shivakumar C.G on 8 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/93918844/
2 2) Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed for ? If so, at what rate and from whom ?
3) What order or award ?
6. The petitioner examined himself as PW.1.
Ex's .
P1 to 14 were marked on his behalf.
The MRO of Essential Hospital, Bengaluru was examined as PW.2 and got marked Ex.15 to 17 document.
In order to prove the defence, the respondent No.2 examined its Senior Executive as RW.1 and got marked Ex.R.1 to 3 documents.
7. Heard erudite counsel for the petitioner and respondents counsels on merits.
Perused the entire materials placed on record.

My answers to the above issues are as follows :-
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.3 : As per final order for the following :
REASONS 8. ISSUE NO.1 : The petitioner has knocked the doors of justice with a relief to grant a compensation of an amount to the tune of Rs.15,00,000/- together.

The evidence on record reveals that after the receipt of complaint lodged by petitioner himself, the jurisdictional police conducted thorough investigation and filed charge sheet against the driver of the car bearing Reg.No.KA-02-MQ-0124 for the offences punishable u/s 279, 337, 338 of IPC and Sec.3(1) r/w 181 of MV Act.
There is nothing on record to believe that the charge sheet filed by the police is defective or collusive.

9. No doubt the respondent No.2 has examined its official as RW.1 has stated that the driver of the car was not possessed valid and effective DL and thereby the police have filed charge sheet against the driver of the car bearing Reg.No.KA-02-MQ- 0124 for the offences punishable u/s 279, 337, 338 of IPC and Sec.3(1) r/w 181 of MV Act.
It is also forthcoming from Ex.P.6 Charge sheet that the driver of the vehicle was not having valid DL at the time of accident.
Be that as it may, the liability will be discussed in the later part of this judgment.

10. It is necessary to reassert that in a claim for compensation filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is expected to prove the incident on basis of principle of preponderance of probabilities and the view taken by this Court is fortified by the decision rendered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others which is reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319.

entities.text: Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Further the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others reported in (2009) 13 SCC 530 has observed that, it is necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.

entities.text: Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others reported in (2009) 13 SCC 530
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The claimants are merely required to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied.

Further the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Krishnappa and another reported in 2001 ACJ 1105,
where the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka considering the fact that the driver of the offending Yatheesha D.H vs Shivakumar C.G on 8 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/93918844/
3 vehicle was not examined to prove any contributory negligence on the part of scooterist held that the accident had occurred due to rash or negligent driving by the driver of the offending van.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Krishnappa and another reported in 2001 ACJ 1105
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Even here in this case the driver of car is not examined to show that there was no negligence on his part and even otherwise the IO, as already observed, has clearly opined that the accident occurred only due to the fault of the driver of car and he was charge sheeted.
On the evidence of PW.1 and Ex.P.7 charge sheet clearly reveals that the accident occurred due to rash and negligence of driver of car.
Though PW.1 was cross- examined at length by respondent No.2 counsel but nothing fatal was elicited so as to distrust the petitioner's version in his chief-examination.
The petitioner has satisfactorily proved that there is a negligence on the part of the driver of car in the accident.

Therefore, this Tribunal answers Issue No.1 'In the Affirmative'.
11. ISSUE NO.2 :
As already discussed above the petitioner has proved that the accident took place due to the actionable negligence of the driver of car.
Therefore he is entitled for compensation.
12. As per the contents of the wound certificate the petitioner has sustained the following injury :(i)
Fracture right clavicle (ii) Abrasion over right forearm
. It is needless to say that the injury No.1 is grievous and injury No.2 is simple in nature.

The Ex.P.8 - Discharge summary issued by Essential Hospital, Bengaluru indicates that the petitioner was treated as an inpatient in the said hospital for the period from 17.03.2020 to 19.03.2020 (4 days in total).
During the course of treatment he had undergone surgeries in the form of : ORIF with clavicle plating done under GA 13.

It is the case of the petitioner that, at the time of accident he was working as Driver in BMTC,
Depot No.34, J.P.Nagar, Bengaluru and was getting salary of Rs.27,000/- p.m.
He further stated that he has become disabled due to the accidental injuries and has lost his earning capacity.
In order to substantiate the above said fact he has produced Ex.P.13 Pay slip and Ex.P.14 ID card.
During the course of his cross examination he admitted that now he was working in Depot No.34, BMTC and prior to the accident also he was working in the same Depot.
He further admitted that he do not have any impediment to produce his salary bank account statement of Canara Bank.
Though PW.1 deposed in his evidence affidavit that due to the injuries sustained in the accident he has lost the future income, but he has not produced any iota of documents.
Non-production of the any documents in this regard results in drawing of an inference that he has not suffered any financial loss during the period of his treatment.
So also the petitioner has not examined the doctor or produced disability certificate to substantiate the fact that he has become permanently disabled.
Under such circumstances, it cannot be accepted that he has suffered permanent disability.

Therefore no compensation is awarded to the petitioner under the heads of 'Loss of future income due to disability' and 'loss of income during laid-up period'.
14.

In this case the petitioner has produced medical bills as per Ex.P9 for having spent Rs.8,771/-
towards medical expenses.
Ex. P.9-
Detailed IP Bill issued by Essential Hospital.
On perusal of the said document it clearly shows that the said bill is duplicate copy.
Further it is discloses that the said amount is reimbursed by Family Health Insurance Plan Ltd.,

Further the total amount is Rs.75,114/-
and the Insurance authorities have paid a sum of Rs.70,114/- and a sum of Rs.5,000/- is paid by petitioner.
All these bills have been examined with care and are found to be correct.

Anyhow because the petitioner has not proved that he has any kind of disability, compensation cannot be Yatheesha D.H vs Shivakumar C.G on 8 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/93918844/
4 awarded under conventional heads.

entities.text: Yatheesha D.H vs Shivakumar C.G on 8 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, the line of treatment and the medical expenses incurred by him, this tribunal is of the view that ends of justice would be met if the petitioner is awarded global compensation of Rs.80,000/-.
15. REGARDING INTEREST & LIABILITY:
Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% per annum is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.
16. There is no dispute with regard to the issuance of insurance policy and its validity as on the date of accident.

The controversy is with regard to the liability of the Insurance Company in the matter of indemnification on the ground that knowing fully well that he had no valid & effective driving licence to drive the car, driver of the car drove the same in violation of the policy conditions and provisions of M.V. Act.
17. Admittedly the insurance policy was issued in respect of a offending car.
But the contents of the charge sheet is available on record as on the date of the accident, the driver was not having driving licence to drove the car.
18. In the light of the discussion made supra, the respondent No.2 has successfully established that the driver of the car did not possess a valid and effective DL at the time of accident.

It is relevant to note that the Insurance Company can be fastened with the liability on the basis of a valid Insurance Policy only after the basic facts are pleaded and established by the owner of the offending vehicle that the said vehicle was not only duly insured but was also driven by an authorized person having a valid DL.
Under such circumstances the burden of proof was upon respondent No.1 to prove that driver had a valid DL at the time of accident.
But in the instant case, for the best reasons known to him the owner of the offending vehicle did not appeared before the court and he was been placed exparte.
As such, an adverse inference is drawn against respondent No.1 that he has consciously violated the terms & conditions of the Insurance policy with regard to the driver's license.

Hence,
the respondent No.2/Insurance company is not liable to indemnify the said insured under the contract of insurance.

19. Now the next question that arises, whether this Tribunal can direct the respondent No.2/Insurance company to pay the award amount together with interest and then recover the same from the insured/respondent No.1.
20

. In this regard respondent No.2 has relied on : (1) MFA-3297/2019 between Smt.
Adilakshmamma and Others v/s Sri. Raju B and another.

entities.text:
Smt.
Adilakshmamma and Others v/s Sri. Raju B and another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
(2) MFA.No.6154/2019 (MV-D) between Hemalatha @ Hema @ Hemavathi and others V/s Bajaj Allianz Gen.Ins.Co.Ltd and another (3)
2018 1 AIR (Kar) (R) 701 and MFA.No.100226/2016 between Padma and others V/s Ramanjali Naidu.

entities.text: Hemalatha @ Hema @ Hemavathi and others V/s Bajaj Allianz Gen.Ins.Co.Ltd
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the above cases the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka observed that if owner of the vehicle violated the condition then owner is only liable to pay the compensation.
The above orders are not reportable and single bench decisions.

In this regard it is worth to rely on the ratio laid down in the decisions cited supra : (1) ILR 2020 KAR 2239 between New India Assurance Co.Ltd Bijapur V/s Yatheesha D.H vs Shivakumar C.G on 8 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/93918844/
5 Yallavva and another, wherein it is held that :
"22.

entities.text: New India Assurance Co.Ltd Bijapur V/s Yatheesha D.H vs Shivakumar C.G
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On a plain reading and meaningful understanding of the above said provision, it is clear that the said provision speaks about the requirements of the policy and the limits of the liability.
Therefore, the liability of the insurer is created under the statute itself which are subject to Sections 149(1) and 149(2) of the Act.

Therefore, the payment of compensation in terms of Section 147(1)
(b), i.e., if the vehicle involved in the accident is duly insured and the insurer has issued any certificate of insurance as provided under sub-Clause 3 of Section 147, the liability of the insurer to satisfy the claim under Section 147(1)(b) is absolute in terms of the policy.

60. Therefore, sub Section (4) and (5) of Section 149 of the Act are enumerated as special contingencies where the statute itself provides the insurer to recover the amount paid under the award by it from the insured.

Apart from that, the apex Court has observed that, under Section 149(2) of the Act, despite the defence taken by the insurer so far as the fundamental breach of conditions are concerned, then also the Tribunal can order for 'pay and recovery'.
But, it all depends upon the facts and circumstance of each case, where the Tribunal has to consider each and every circumstances of a case before passing such an order of 'pay and recovery'.
In view of the above decision it clears that, even the insured violated the conditions insurer has to pay and thereafter recover the same from the owner.
If there as dispute about the involvement of the vehicle and allegations in this regard
then only the owner is liable.
21. In the decision of (2018) 9 SCC 650 between Shamanna V/s Oriental Ins.Co.Ltd., and (2022) 1 SCC 317 in the case of Kurvan Ansari Alias Kurvan Ali and another V/s Shayam Kishore Murmu and another.

entities.text: Kurvan Ansari Alias Kurvan Ali and another V/s Shayam Kishore Murmu and another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the above decisions Hon'ble Apex Court held that : even the owner violated the condition the duty of the insurer to satisfy the award and recover the same from the owner.

Accordingly this Tribunal intends that it is just and proper to direct the insurer i.e., Respondent No.2 to pay the amount together with interest @ 6% p.a, from the date of claim petition till realization of entire award amount to the petitioner herein.
However the respondent No.2 is at liberty to recover the award amount together with the interest so paid, from the insured/ Respondent No.1
in appropriate execution proceedings as held in Oriental Insurance Co.Ltd V/s Nanjappan & others, reported in (2004) 13 SCC 224.

entities.text: Oriental Insurance Co.Ltd V/s Nanjappan & others, reported in (2004) 13 SCC 224
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: With this observation, issue No.2 is answered as 'Partly in the affirmative'.
22. ISSUE NO.3 :

In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
ORDER

The petition filed under Section 166 of M.V. Act 1988, is hereby partly allowed with costs in the following terms :
The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.80,000/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire award amount.
Yatheesha D.H vs Shivakumar C.G on 8 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/93918844/
6

The respondent No.2 is hereby directed to pay the aforesaid award amount together with interest to the petitioner within two months from the date of this order, with liberty to recover the same from the insured/respondent No.1 in appropriate execution proceedings as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Oriental Insurance Company Ltd V/s Nanjappan & others reported in (2004) 13 SCC 224.

entities.text: Oriental Insurance Company Ltd V/s Nanjappan & others reported in (2004) 13 SCC 224
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Out of the above said compensation amount awarded to the petitioner, 80% of the award amount with accrued interest shall be paid to him through NEFT/RTGS by way of E-payment on proper identification and due verification and further 20% of the award amount shall be kept in FD in favour of petitioner in any Nationalized or Scheduled bank for a period of 3 years.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
